suggestedQuestions.text: Why does the armature current go up when excitation changes?
Why doesn't the motor speed change with excitation?
What does unity power factor mean for this motor?

chunks.title: Constant speed
chunks.text: A synchronous motor locks onto the rotating field of the supply. Its speed depends only on supply frequency and pole count, never on the load.

chunks.title: Phasor view
chunks.text: To see what the machine does electrically, we draw voltages and currents as phasors. Lengths show size, and angles show timing.

chunks.title: Back EMF
chunks.text: The spinning rotor field induces a back EMF, called E, in the stator windings. The supply voltage V and E together decide the armature current.

chunks.title: Field excitation
chunks.text: Excitation is the DC current we feed the rotor field winding. More excitation means a stronger rotor field, and so a larger back EMF.

chunks.title: Armature current
chunks.text: At a fixed load the motor must draw the same real power. So the part of the armature current that is in phase with V stays constant.

chunks.title: Power factor
chunks.text: Excitation only reshapes the reactive part. Under-excited, the current lags the voltage. Over-excited, it leads. At unity, current is smallest.

chunks.title: The V-curve
chunks.text: Plot armature current against excitation and you get a V. The bottom of the V is unity power factor, where the current is at its minimum.

chunks.title: Load angle
chunks.text: As the load rises, E slips further behind V. That angle is the load angle, and it must stay below ninety degrees to keep the motor in step.

misconceptions.label: Excitation adds power
misconceptions.description: Raising excitation makes the motor draw more real power, so the armature current rises because the motor is 'working harder'.

misconceptions.label: Only load sets current
misconceptions.description: Armature current can only change when the mechanical load changes; field excitation cannot affect it.

misconceptions.label: Excitation changes speed
misconceptions.description: Changing the field current changes how fast the motor turns, as in a DC motor.

misconceptions.label: Unity PF means max current
misconceptions.description: Unity power factor is thought to be the point of maximum current, instead of the minimum for a given load.
signals: best power factor means most current

misconceptions.label: Current always in phase
misconceptions.description: The armature current is assumed to always be in phase with the supply voltage, so there is no reactive component to adjust.
